target: flower (PO_0009046) as bearer, with the series position 'outer' as bearer state (pattern 04); the count goes to the flower
reason: A floret is a flower (PO lists floret as a synonym of PO_0009046, and the previous review used that rule, C261); 'outer' is a position in the head, not a different structure. It is not always a ray flower (PO_0025331): in disciform heads the outer florets are filiform female florets, so mapping to ray flower would be wrong. The position values (upper/lower/inner/outer/lateral) are still pending in pattern 04, so these rows wait for them.

A counting unit in moss descriptions ('2-stratose in 1-3 cell rows', 'of 4-6 rows of cells'): the number of cell rows is a width measure of the border or costa that is being described. The bearer is that border or costa, and the number of rows is its quality; 'cell row' is not a bearer itself.

'Appendage' of the corolla covers different structures: faucal scales or fornices (Boraginaceae, which could go to corolline corona FLOPO_0985021), infrastaminal scales, spurs and appendages of the lobes. The examples (2 or 2-4 appendages, multicellular, linear to conical) do not tell which one is meant. A floral corona class would be a doubtful target without the family.

target: glume (PO_0009039) with the region 'margin' (region-of-the-bearer pattern, as with other organ margins)
reason: The margin of an existing class. Hyaline, scarious, erose and ciliate are margin qualities of the glume. PO has margin classes only for leaf, carpel and stamen, so it is expressed as a region of the glume.

Narrower in use. The examples 'auricles and oral setae absent' and 'weak, fragile' are bamboo and grass sheath auricles, which is PO_0020106 exactly. Contextual only (like the awn rule): use it for Poaceae/Cyperaceae leaf sheaths. In dicots 'auricles' of the blade base are lobes of the leaf lamina base, not this class, and the French 'aiguës, acuminées' may be that sense.

label: cirrus
parent: is_a leaf rachis (PO_0020055); part_of vascular leaf (PO_0009025)
definition: A leaf rachis that extends beyond the uppermost leaflets as a long, leafless, whip-like and non-coiling extension armed with grapnel-like spines, by which climbing palms (rattans) attach to supports.
reason: A main palm character (cirrus present/absent, length, shape) found in three floras. The PO tendrils (leaf rachis tendril PO_0025366, leaf apex tendril PO_0025363) are defined as coiling, which a cirrus is not, so they would be wrong. The flagellum (a sterile inflorescence arising from the sheath) is a different organ: 'spiny climbing whips arising from...' is probably a flagellum and should not get this class. Propose to PO upstream.

Narrower. A monochasium is a cyme with one branch at each node. PO uses 'monochasium' as a synonym on several kinds (bostryx PO_0030134, cincinnus PO_0030132, rhipidium PO_0030131, anthela, corymb), so no single one of those is right. Their common parent, cyme inflorescence, is.

target: flower (PO_0009046) with the series position 'outer' as bearer state (pattern 04)
reason: Same as 'outer floret': florets at the edge of a head, which are ray, filiform-female or bilabiate depending on the head. So the position is stated, not ray flower. It waits for the pending position values.

Narrower. In Passiflora the limen is the inner annular or cup-shaped part of the extrastaminal corona complex round the base of the androgynophore. The French source itself calls it 'couronne interne (limen)'. It is limited to one family, so it does not need its own class.

label: vaginant lamina
parent: is_a cardinal organ part (PO_0025001); part_of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075)
definition: A portion of a non-vascular leaf of Fissidens and related mosses formed by two lamina flaps on the adaxial side of the proximal leaf, which clasp the stem and the base of the next leaf above.
reason: 'Vagrant' is a misspelling of 'vaginant'. 'Vaginant laminae equal/unequal' is a standard Fissidens character in three moss floras. The two flaps are compared with each other, which needs its own bearer. FLOPO equal/unequal (FLOPO:0991102/0991101) then apply. Propose to PO upstream, which covers moss leaves.
Part of an arrangement phrase ('flowers 7-9 per spiral'). The bearer is the flower and the count is per spiral of the axis.
French 'or' (alternatives, pattern 07), not a word for a plant part.

Narrower. In the examples (Loranthaceae/Viscaceae: 'pairs of opposite dyads', 'umbel of 2 dyads') a dyad is a two-flowered partial inflorescence, a cymule. PO lists cymule as a synonym of cyme inflorescence. Only for inflorescence context: a pollen dyad is a different thing.
A unit, not a part: overlap, moisture content, viability.

label: carpopodium
parent: is_a cardinal organ part (PO_0025001); part_of cypsela (FLOPO_0986053)
definition: A cardinal organ part at the base of a cypsela formed by a distinct ring or pad of differentiated, often sclerified cells, by which the fruit is attached to the receptacle and from which it separates.
reason: A standard Asteraceae fruit character (present, shape, symmetry, colour) used by several floras. It has no PO class, and fruit columella or gynophore (PO_0004540, PO_0006330, PO lists 'carpophore') are different organs. Propose to PO upstream together with cypsela.

target: lemma (PO_0009037) with the series position 'upper' as bearer state (pattern 04)
reason: The lemma of the upper floret of the spikelet, which is a position in a series. In Paniceae it is usually the fertile lemma (PO_0009041), but not in all grasses, so the position is stated. It waits for the pending position values.

target: glume (PO_0009039) part of spikelet (PO_0009051) with quality male (pattern 12, part of a qualified whole)
reason: The glume of male (staminate) spikelets. The glume is the part and 'male' qualifies the whole spikelet, as in 'calyx of male flowers'.
Part of a count phrase ('lateral nerves up to 8 on either side of the midrib'). The bearer is the vein and 'on either side' says how it is counted.

Exact or close synonym: a vein running just inside and along the leaf margin, formed by joined secondary loops. That matches the PO definition (just inside the lamina margin, from base to apex). The French 'paires de nervures submarginales' are the same structure.

target: staminal tube (FLOPO_0986013) with PATO lobed; the number of lobes as a count of parts (pattern 03), as with '10-lobed'
reason: These are the apical lobes or appendages of the Meliaceae staminal tube. Counts ('surmonté de 10 lobes') are a lobed staminal tube with a number. Shape and length of single lobes (conic, obtuse, 1.5-2 mm) cannot be expressed without a lobe class. Those rows stay unresolved until more floras show the class is needed.
A bad split of the French 'fois' (times), as in '2 fois bifurqué' and '3-4 fois ramifiées'. It is a degree of branching or division, or a ratio, not a part.

Exact. French for furrow or groove. PO canal is 'a groove on the surface, or a tube in the interior' and has furrow, groove, sulcus and vallecula as synonyms. The counts ('5 sillons longitudinaux') are counts of canals on the organ.
A quality of arrangement (crowded pairs of pinnae or leaflets), not a part.
Part of a ratio to another part ('2 times as long as the sepals'), handled by pattern 10 with sepal (PO_0009031) as the other part.

Narrower. The examples ('4 extrorse-lateral cells', 'third whorl', introrse or extrorse) are Lauraceae anthers, whose 2 or 4 'cells' are separate pollen sacs opening by valves. In 2-celled anthers of other families 'cell' can mean the theca (PO_0009069), so map to the pollen sac only where cells are counted as 4 or opening by valves. Otherwise use anther theca.

target: capitulum inflorescence (PO_0030121) with bearer state female (pattern 04, as 'male flowers')
reason: A capitulum in a female state. Keeping the capitulum is more specific than pistillate inflorescence (PO_0025598). The count goes to the capitulum.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075), region margin (pattern 12 with the region of the whole)
reason: These are cells of the leaf border (limbidium) of mosses, a region of an existing class, and papillose/hyaline/rectangular are cell qualities. PO has no margin class for the non-vascular leaf, so the margin is a region of the leaf.

'Lip' is either the corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017, sympetalous families) or the orchid labellum (a petal; there is no labellum class, only labellum lobe FLOPO_0986028). 'Limb' is then the expanded blade of either. The examples (semiorbicular, dentate, 3-4 mm) do not tell which family.

label: teniola
parent: is_a portion of plant tissue (PO_0009007); part_of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075)
definition: A portion of plant tissue of a non-vascular leaf of Calymperaceae mosses forming a longitudinal band of elongate, thick-walled, often hyaline cells within the leaf lamina, between the costa and the margin.
reason: A real, named moss leaf structure (present/absent, conspicuous, interrupted) used for Syrrhopodon/Calymperes in three floras. It is not the border or the costa (PO_0030072). Propose to PO upstream with the moss leaf terms.

Unclear structure: it could be anther tubules (as in Ericaceae: 'slender, upcurved, 1-2 mm long'), whose bearer is a tube-shaped outgrowth of the theca, or a dehiscence channel. PO canal (PO_0025132) is a space and would be wrong for a solid tubule. More context is needed.
